reviews.title: Promising Idea, Frustrating Realit
reviews.text:
Fabulous markets itself as a tool to help people improve their lives, build healthier habits, and achieve personal growth. Unfortunately, my experience left me feeling like the company is far more focused on collecting subscription payments than delivering meaningful value.

The app itself was underwhelming and didn’t justify the cost. However, my biggest disappointment was the company’s billing and cancellation practices. I had already contacted Fabulous directly requesting cancellation before seeking additional help. Despite my efforts, I continued experiencing billing issues, including multiple successful charges through a different billing source after blocking the original one.

I finally received confirmation of cancellation on September 16, 2026, yet 45 days later, on October 31, I received another email informing me my subscription had been canceled, with an outstanding invoice of $39.99.

After researching other customer experiences, I discovered similar complaints about billing, cancellations, and disappointing subscription value. My experience certainly doesn’t appear to be unique.

For a company built around helping people take control of their lives and improve their well-being, the frustration involved in simply trying to cancel a subscription is particularly disappointing.

I wanted to invest in myself, but instead felt like I was investing in a company’s subscription revenue.

Fabulous does an excellent job marketing the promise of self-improvement. Unfortunat

reviews.title: A wellness company that made an already difficult situation worse
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed by my experience with Fabulous, particularly its subscription management and customer service.

I signed up for a trial in July 2026 but did not use the app afterwards. Despite this, Fabulous charged me £34.99 on 28 July and another £34.99 on 28 September, in addition to an initial £0.89 payment.

I paid £70.87 for a service I did not use.

I only reinstalled the app to investigate the charges and establish how to cancel my subscription.
I found the subscription management process unnecessarily complicated. My account appeared to show a free subscription, yet I was being charged for a premium plan. It took considerable effort to locate my billing history and establish what I had been paying for.

What makes this particularly disappointing is that I have significant visual impairment following multiple retinal surgeries and ongoing specialist hospital treatment.

These medical circumstances have affected my ability to manage everyday administrative tasks, including subscriptions.

I explained this to Fabulous, alongside my financial hardship, and requested a compassionate review of the most recent £34.99 charge.

My request was rejected twice.

Rather than meaningfully addressing the accessibility difficulties I described, customer service repeatedly referred me to the company’s subscription terms.

I accept that I originally agreed to a trial. However, I believe companies offering wellness and self-improvement services should demonstrate some under

reviews.title: Misleading Subscriptions and an Unnecessarily Difficult Cancellation Process
reviews.text:
Be very careful when signing up for Fabulous.

I paid one dollar and signed up for a free trial and unexpectedly received FOUR separate subscription confirmation emails, each with a different subscription ID and its own billing information.

When I tried to cancel, the official website showed me as an "Active Free User," with no paid subscriptions listed. I had to figure out how to locate and manage subscriptions that weren't even visible in the account dashboard.

The subscriptions can technically be canceled, but the cancellation process is unnecessarily confusing and difficult.

To make matters worse, the confirmation emails ask you to "Activate Your Subscription," making it sound like billing hasn't started, even though the subscriptions are set to automatically renew unless canceled.

Why should customers have to go through so much trouble just to find out what they're subscribed to and how to cancel?

My advice: Check every subscription confirmation email carefully. Don't assume you're safe just because your account says "Free User." Fabulous seriously needs to improve its subscription transparency and cancellation experience.

reviews.title: Questionable Subscription Practices for an ADHD Focused Ap
reviews.text:
For an app marketed toward people with ADHD, who may struggle with forgetfulness, administrative tasks, and follow-through, I find it troubling that Fabulous continues collecting subscription payments on long-dormant accounts without any apparent safeguards or flexibility.

In my case, I was charged $40 every other month for an account that had been inactive for over a year. Despite the lack of activity, customer support was unwilling to offer any refund.

While consumers are ultimately responsible for managing their subscriptions, I would expect a company serving this particular audience to demonstrate greater awareness of these challenges. Instead, these practices feel exploitative of the very people the app claims to support.

Consider this a cautionary tale: if you try Fabulous, make sure you have a reliable system for tracking and canceling your subscription.

reviews.title: Preys on people looking for help
reviews.text:
Misleading subscription design – particularly concerning for an app targeting ADHD and burnout

I downloaded Fabulous after being specifically targeted with advertising suggesting it could help with ADHD and burnout. Unfortunately, my experience of the app has been the opposite.

The set-up process feels deliberately designed to blur the line between simply progressing through onboarding and committing to additional paid subscriptions. I was repeatedly presented with what appeared to be “next steps”, only to find they were actually one-click subscription commitments to additional services/apps. For something specifically marketed towards people who may already struggle with overwhelm, attention and executive function, I find this particularly troubling.

Once subscribed, figuring out exactly what I had signed up for and how to cancel was a complicated maze. The sheer number of prompts, offers and additional subscription opportunities made the whole experience feel less like onboarding and more like a carefully designed sales funnel.

Having gone through all of that, what I seem to have ended up with is essentially a very expensive reminder to drink water.

I appreciate that subscription apps need to make money, but users should understand clearly when they are making a purchase, what they are purchasing and how much it will cost. In my experience, that clarity was completely lacking.

I would like the subscriptions I inadvertently signed up for through this process cancelled

Spoiler: hidden subscriptions and complicated cancellation process. £100 has been taken out of my account despite me believing I had unsubscribed.

Having been struggling with ADHD I fell for the slick instagram adverts and was excited to give Fabulous a go. I started a one week trial and then downloaded Clarity as well because this was pushed to me by the app as the one you actually need for ADHD. 

Firstly, the apps are so busy there’s way too much going on and the duo-lingo gamification meant I would have to work up to being able to just have a simple weekly routine checklist put together. So I cancelled - or so I thought - my subscriptions days before the free trial ended. 

Jump to now, where several payments from thefab.co have been taken out of my account totalling over £100. Apparently, during the process of signing up, ON THE APP, I had also made several additional subscriptions to all these other platforms via the website - the subscriptions do not show when you look on the App Store and are conveniently hidden on the website. 

I’m so angry and upset, that in trying to feel more on top of my life I’ve been totally taken advantage of. I will be trying to get a refund if anyone else has successfully done so let me know.

reviews.title: Preying on vulnerable people
reviews.text:
After seeing ads for this app dozens of times every day presenting itself as the solution for people struggling with ADHD, designed by academics, I caved and said I’d try it for just under a pound. As a disabled and chronically ill person, I do not have a lot of money to spare on something that won’t even really tell me what it is and simply promises to change my life. Instead of learning more during the sign-up process, I mostly remember it just being a series of upsells for yet more vague apps and subscriptions.
I did my best to find how to decline the upsell again and again and when I finally got to try out the app, I quickly realised that it would not work for me. Before being able to do anything else, you need to make a solemn promise to yourself that includes remembering every day that you are going to die. I do not need that kind of anxiety trigger and it suggested a vibe of pressure to be productive to me that is not compatible with taking care of my mental health while chronically ill.
I ended up deleting the app and thought that was that until I see a month later that 35 pounds have been taken from my bank account. I was not aware of committing to a subscription that would 40x in price between month 1 and 2 and I did not receive any communication in advance of the renewal or debiting my account. In order to find how to cancel the subscription, I had to re-download the app and go through another five-minute tutorial before being able to navigate to my account setting

I emailed a third time and demanding a refund or I will go to my bank, and I got the same response again saying that they will not give me a refund. So now I have to go to my bank and try to get three months worth of subscriptions refunded to my account and I will have to change my debit card number in to prevent this from happening in the future. If I go to the site right now and try to cancel I can’t because I canceled three months ago. 

Update: It took months and dozens of emails back-and-forth to get two out of three of the $50 charges refunded to my account. I had to threaten to go to my bank and get the charges reversed. After several months, they finally told me that somehow when I subscribed to one product, I ended up with a subscription to multiple other products, which was never my intent, and that’s why when I thought I canceled the service, I didn’t cancel everything. I stand by my origina

After blocking my card, not knowing what was going on they are allegedly refunding me within 10 days. My bank blocked the transactions luckily and I kept my money.

I’m outraged this is allowed to happen in the App Store and I’ll be petitioning for its removal. They are committing pure theft.

The reply is an absolute joke. I found out they charged me for additional apps I NEVER DOWNLOADED! That’s not in your terms and conditions, it’s fraud and theft. Transparency? You’re outright thieves and it’s a disgrace you’re still allowed to operate.

reviews.title: Predatory Subscription
reviews.text: This app is creepy and I don't like it. I have autism and ADHD and downloaded it on a whim, opened it, saw all of the pop ups and tutorials, and immediately got overwhelmed. I think I paid a couple dollars to "try it out" and then it charged my card for a premium subscription the next month once I had already forgotten about it. After ignoring the app and its repetitive notifications for about two months without opening it, I finally fought my task avoidance enough to open it and cancel my subscription. This took like ten minutes for me to do, because it's hidden in a menu, and it pulls up a pop-up within the app that I couldn't access with my VPN on, so I had to turn that off. And the app has so many pop-up tutorial and other notifications that I kept having to swipe away. Once I finally found the correct settings to cancel my membership, the first time I tried to, it only paused it for two months. I had to click through the entire cancel screen (with an offer to keep my membership for a lower price, which also gave me The Ick) to properly get rid of my membership and promptly uninstall the app. If you actually have a mental disability on the level of ADHD and/or autism, I would highly advise you not to install this app like I did, because of these predatory behaviors. It unsettles me greatly that this app is designed the way that it is for a demographic of people that are usually much more susceptible to falling into traps like these.

reviews.title: SCAM
reviews.text: First of all…. When a person reads the reviews and how they are either starting the same feeling I experienced…. Scam, horrible customer service, difficult to cancel, unauthorized charges, etc… then the other half just praise this app, it leads one to believe that the positive reviews are FAKE.  I believe the one star reviews and call bs on the positive ones.  No app can have such hot/cold reviews unless some of them are FAKE.  you can tell ask the negative reviews are legit because they all describe the same thing I experienced and that this app should be held liable for all the unhonored refund requests and return all the charges fraudulently made without our authorization.  Kinds of ironic this is an app designed to increase our daily motivation & willpower, yet the creator has intentionally caused us frustration and stress that counteracts any good this app may have brought forth.  I have been being charged for this app since May 2025 I have never initiated any subscription to this app and when I try to call customer service, they are very rude and deny me a refund. There is nowhere on my Apple account where I have initiated this app and I only just downloaded it so I could leave a review warning other people to stay away from this app. It’s a scam and they intentionally deceive you.  Their customer service leaves a lot to be desired to say the least.
